subproblem.title: Hoelder bounds pass to pointwise limits, and the limit is continuous
subproblem.statement: Let n, l be natural numbers, L := L(R^n, R^l) with the operator norm, alpha > 0 and K >= 0 real, F_j : R^n -> L (j in N) and V : R^n -> L with F_j(z) -> V(z) for every z in R^n. Assume that for all z, z' in R^n, ||F_j(z) - F_j(z')|| <= K |z - z'|^alpha for all sufficiently large j. Then ||V(z) - V(z')|| <= K |z - z'|^alpha for all z, z' in R^n, and V is continuous.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (α K : ℝ) (F : ℕ → Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ)) (V : Rn n → (Rn n →L[ℝ] Rn ℓ)), 0 < α → 0 ≤ K → (∀ z, Tendsto (fun j => F j z) atTop (𝓝 (V z))) → (∀ z z' : Rn n, ∀ᶠ j in atTop, ‖F j z - F j z'‖ ≤ K * ‖z - z'‖ ^ α) → (∀ z z' : Rn n, ‖V z - V z'‖ ≤ K * ‖z - z'‖ ^ α) ∧ Continuous V
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 7b-c of the parent proof, stated for a general pointwise convergent sequence.
1. Hoelder bound. Fix z, z' in R^n. By pointwise convergence, F_j(z) - F_j(z') -> V(z) - V(z'). By continuity of the norm, ||F_j(z) - F_j(z')|| -> ||V(z) - V(z')|| (Tendsto.sub, Tendsto.norm). By hypothesis these real numbers are at most c := K |z - z'|^alpha for all large j. The interval (-infinity, c] is closed, so the limit also satisfies ||V(z) - V(z')|| <= K |z - z'|^alpha (le_of_tendsto).
2. Continuity. Fix z.
 a. The map t -> K t^alpha is continuous at t = 0, because alpha > 0 (Real.continuousAt_rpow_const 0 alpha, using 0 <= alpha), and its value there is K * 0^alpha = 0 (Real.zero_rpow). The map z' -> |z' - z| is continuous with value 0 at z' = z. So K |z' - z|^alpha -> 0 as z' -> z.
 b. By step 1, 0 <= ||V(z') - V(z)|| <= K |z' - z|^alpha for every z'. By the squeeze theorem (squeeze_zero), ||V(z') - V(z)|| -> 0, that is, V(z') -> V(z) as z' -> z (tendsto_iff_norm_sub_tendsto_zero).
 c. So V is continuous at every point, hence continuous (continuous_iff_continuousAt). QED.
proof_key_steps: ||F_j(z) - F_j(z')|| -> ||V(z) - V(z')|| and is eventually <= K|z - z'|^alpha, so the limit obeys the same bound
K|z' - z|^alpha -> 0 as z' -> z because alpha > 0
the squeeze theorem gives continuity of V at every point

audit.reason: The exact type correctly permits the eventual threshold to depend on the pair of points. Pointwise convergence, continuous subtraction and norm, and closedness of the real order bound establish the global Holder estimate. Positivity of alpha makes the comparison function vanish at zero; squeezing proves continuity everywhere. The supplied proof is complete and has no child or parent dependencies.
